metadata.subject: Algorithms
metadata.title: Discover Breadth-First Search
metadata.description: Traverse a graph level by level with a queue of waiting nodes.

learning_objectives: Explain a graph and a starting node.
Track the BFS queue and visited nodes.

mission.title: Visit by levels
mission.description: Use the queue to visit the start node, then its neighbors, one level at a time.

introduction.title: BFS explores nearby nodes first
introduction.content: Breadth-First Search (BFS) starts at one graph node and uses a queue to visit all nearby nodes before moving farther away.
points: A graph is made of nodes and connections.
Visited nodes are not added twice.
The queue's front determines the next visit.

worked_example.title: Follow the queue
worked_example.content: Starting at A, add its neighbors to the back of the queue.

steps.explanation: A is visited first; its neighbors B and C join the queue.

steps.visual: Visited: A → B | Queue: C → D → E
steps.explanation: B leaves the front, and its unvisited neighbors D and E join the back.

steps.visual: Visited: A → B → C → D → E
steps.explanation: The queue keeps the traversal in level order.

worked_example.conclusion: BFS reaches every node at the current distance before going deeper.

next.title: Now traverse the graph.
next.content: Watch the queue and visited list change together.

next-step: A is the starting node, so it is visited first.
The next node comes from the front of the queue.
Unvisited neighbors join the back of the queue.
BFS has visited every reachable node.

prediction.heading: After visiting A…
prediction.question: Which node will BFS visit next from the queue?
prediction.selection_message: Your prediction: {prediction}. Continue BFS to check it.
prediction.required_message: Choose the next node BFS will visit.

result.actual: BFS visits {actual} next from the front of the queue.

actions.label: Visit the start node
actions.task: Choose the start node to put its neighbors into the queue.

actions.label: Visit the next level
actions.task: Choose the node at the front of the queue.

actions.label: Visit the remaining neighbors
actions.task: Keep visiting nodes in queue-front order.

actions.label: Continue the queue
actions.task: Add unvisited neighbors to the back before choosing again.

challenge.title: BFS challenge
challenge.start_message: Traverse from A while keeping the queue in level order.
challenge.continue_message: Challenge complete. Replay BFS by choosing nodes from the queue.

phases.title: Visit every node
phases.instruction: Choose each node in breadth-first order by following the front of the queue.
phases.feedback: Always take the next node from the front of the queue.

guidance.start_message: Choose the next node at the front of the BFS queue.

items.content: Visit A, then add B and C before going deeper.

phases.title: Practise the BFS queue
phases.instruction: Select and confirm nodes in level order.
phases.feedback: The queue's front is the next node to visit.

guidance.start_message: Apply level-order traversal without a hint.

phases.title: Apply BFS
phases.instruction: Traverse the new graph one queue-front node at a time.
phases.feedback: Add neighbors to the back, but visit from the front.

guidance.start_message: Traverse the unfamiliar graph without hints.

phases.title: Solve the traversal
phases.instruction: Reach every node in BFS order.
phases.feedback: When B is visited, C is already waiting in the queue.

guidance.start_message: Master level-order traversal on this unfamiliar graph.

phases.title: Master BFS
phases.instruction: Predict and confirm every queue-front visit.
phases.feedback: BFS visits by distance from the start node.

thinking.title: Predict the BFS queue
thinking.instruction: Mentally follow the queue and predict the visit order.
thinking.do_not_execute: Do not click the graph yet. Follow the queue from front to back.

prediction_fields.label: Visit order
prediction_fields.prompt: Which nodes will BFS visit, in order?

feedback.incorrect: Keep the queue order: finish the current level before going deeper.

solve.title: Expert BFS
solve.instruction: Traverse the generated graph without hints.

quiz.question: What determines the next node visited by BFS?

discovery.title: BFS discovery
discovery.summary: BFS uses a queue to finish nearby levels before it explores farther nodes.

sections.title: What?
sections.content: BFS explores a graph level by level from a chosen start node.

sections.title: Example
sections.content: From A, visit A, then B and C, then D and E.

sections.title: Why?
sections.content: A queue preserves the order that keeps nearby nodes ahead of deeper nodes.

sections.title: Remember
sections.content: Visit front → add unvisited neighbors to the back.

alternate_explanations.title: Think of ripples
alternate_explanations.content: A drop in water reaches the closest ring first, then the next ring farther out.

alternate_explanations.title: Walk through it
alternate_explanations.content: Start A, queue B and C; visit B, queue D and E; then visit C, D, and E.

recall.title: Recall
recall.prompt: In your own words, why does BFS use a queue?
recall.model_answer: The queue visits nodes in arrival order, so all neighbors at the current level are handled before deeper nodes.
